newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - April 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - April 4.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Perth Reds Super League player Mark Geyer was suspended for ten matches after an emotional Super League judiciary hearing. Geyer was found guilty of eye gouging and a reckless high tackle and has seven days to lodge an appeal. Page 20.

Australian cricket reserve wicket-keeper Adam Gilchrist may replace an injured Mark Waugh in the next one-day match in South Africa. Waugh remains in doubt for the rest of the series but is unlikely to return home early. Page 20.

AFL side Richmond has named fullback Scott Turner for his first game in nearly a year. Surgery on a kneecap and a long rehabilitation process threatened his playing future, but he will take on Adelaide star player Tony Modra in Melbourne tomorrow. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australia begins a Davis Cup tie against the Czech Republic today at White City, Melbourne. Mark Philippoussis and Pat Rafter play in the singles today, with Todd Woodbridge and Mark Woodforde playing doubles tomorrow. The winner of the tie plays the winer of the United States-Netherlands quarter-final. Page 40.

The National Netball League is facing strike action by its players if a contract dispute is not settled today. Players will address issues including copyright, intellectual property and compensation at a meeting with League officials. Page 39.

The Gold Coast Indy Car Championship starts today with the first of the qualifying rounds. Leading driver Alex Zanardi's plans for a six consecutive Indy pole position are in doubt after he contracted conjunctivitis. Page 37.
THE AGE

Carlton AFL player and dual Brownlow medallist Greg Williams will lose at least A$100,000 in earnings as a result of his nine-match suspension for pushing an umpire. Carlton president John Elliott has repeated a threat for further court action. Page D3.

In a crackdown on player misbehaviour, the Australian Football League has stopped players doing victory laps to thank supporters by instructing them to leave the field immediately once the game has finished. The league is extending rules to segregate teas wherever possible. Page D3.

The head of sport at ABC Radio Neville Oliver has walked out on indefinite leave over ABC management plans threatening broadcasts of AFL football and cricket. The ABC plans could effect the broadcasting of rural, religious and sporting programmes. Page D11
THE HERALD SUN

Australian cricketer Shane Warne has declared that the forthcoming Ashes tour of England may be his last and that he may quit the game early due to the pressures of the game. Warne believes he is mentally tired and may retire to pursue State cricket with Victoria. Page 92.

Geelong AFL player Gary Ablett has refused to undergo surgery on an injured knee which may have prolonged his career. Ablett has partially torn a cruciate ligament and will not play for six to eight weeks. Page 100.

Basketball player Mark Bradtke has been refused permission from his American NBA club the Philadelphia 76ers to return to his Australian side, the Melbourne Tigers. Bradtke has had a tough season with the 76ers, who will not reach the play-offs. Page 89.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Racing trainer John Hawkes and owners Jack and Bob Ingham are intent on retiring popular horse Octagonal, despite a public appeal for the horse to keep racing. A Queensland-wide petition is circulating to extend Octagonal's career past the Queen Elizabet Stakes on April 12. Page 118.

The Sydney grade cricket final will be held this weekend between St George and Mosman. St George all-rounder Brad McNamara will play as a batsman only after recent groin surgery, while Mosman will be relying on State players Shane Lee and Phil Alley. Pag 117.
Round five in the Australian Rugby League competition continues tonight, with Manly playing Sydney City at Brookvale Oval. Manly captain Geoff Toovey will play in his 200th grade game. Page 110.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
